subtitle: Lesson 108 · Transactions, Locking, and Isolation Levels

eyebrow: How big is the thing being locked?
code:
-- Row:   a single row            -- most granular
-- Page:  an 8KB page (many rows)  -- middle ground
-- Table: the entire table         -- least granular
caption: Three sizes of resource, each lock type can be taken on any of them.

eyebrow: The trade-off runs in opposite directions
code:
-- Row lock:   BEST concurrency,  MOST overhead at scale
-- Table lock: LEAST overhead,    WORST concurrency
-- Page lock:  a middle ground on both axes
caption: A table lock blocks rows the holder never even looked at.

eyebrow: A single-row UPDATE vs. a bulk one
code:
-- Small, targeted: typically a row lock
UPDATE Production.Product SET ListPrice = 25.00
WHERE ProductID = 680;

-- Large fraction of the table: optimizer may
-- choose page or table locking instead
UPDATE Production.Product SET ListPrice = ListPrice * 1.05
WHERE ProductLine = 'R';
caption: Same lock TYPE, different GRANULARITY, chosen by cost.

code:
-- No GRANULARITY keyword exists in T-SQL.
-- SQL Server picks it from estimated rows touched,
-- table/index structure, and current conditions.
caption: Based on cost estimates, not a setting you control directly.
